questions.question: The <label for='email'> associates with an input via the input's:
questions.explanation: for must equal the target input's id. Proper labels improve a11y and clickable area.

questions.question: To send form data via the URL (GET) vs body (POST), you use:
questions.explanation: method controls how data is submitted; GET appends to URL (idempotent, bookmarkable), POST sends in body (for mutations).

questions.question: The 'name' attribute on an input is important because it:

options.text: Identifies the field's key in submitted form data

questions.explanation: Only inputs with a name are submitted; name becomes the key (e.g. email=value) in the payload.

questions.question: required on an input:

options.text: Blocks native form submission until the field is filled

questions.explanation: The required attribute triggers built-in browser validation before submit — no JS needed for the basic check.

questions.question: The 'placeholder' attribute shows:

options.text: Hint text inside the field that disappears on input (not a label substitute)

questions.explanation: Placeholder is a hint only; always provide a real <label> for accessibility — placeholders vanish and aren't announced as labels.

questions.question: A fieldset/legend is useful for:

options.text: Grouping related controls with an accessible group label

questions.explanation: fieldset + legend semantically groups radios/checkboxes and is announced by screen readers as a group.

questions.question: For accessibility, each input should have:
questions.explanation: A real label (or aria-label) lets screen readers announce the field's purpose; placeholder/title alone is insufficient.

questions.question: novalidate on a <form> does:

options.text: Disables native browser validation (lets you handle it in JS)

questions.explanation: novalidate skips built-in checks — useful when you run custom Angular/JS validation and don't want double prompts.
